March 2026 U.S. consumer price index (CPI) data was released on April 10, 2026, at 8:30 A.M. ET, showing an annual inflation rate of 3.3% and a 0.9% increase for the month. This report indicates a rise from February's 2.4% rate, largely driven by energy costs, with the next release scheduled for May 12, 2026. March 2026 CPI Data Highlights Annual Inflation (YoY): 3.3% (up from 2.4% in Feb). Monthly Change (MoM): +0.9% (up from +0.3% in Feb). Core CPI (ex-food/energy): +2.6% annually. Driver: Significant surge in energy costs. Key Takeaways Market Reaction: Stocks rose following the report, with market participants seeing improved odds of a Fed rate cut. Expert Concerns: The data reflects the first full impact of the Iran war's energy shock on US gasoline prices, which exceeded $4 per gallon. Upcoming Data: The next release, featuring April 2026 data, is scheduled for May 12, 2026. The Bureau of Labor Statistics maintains the official schedule.
